title: Buffered document indexing with snapshot publishing
name: Index refresh coordinator

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code maintains the pending-document counter while documents are being added and refreshes run? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
compact() and refresh() can both publish a new snapshot. If compact() builds its merged snapshot from a stale prev and a refresh publishes first, what happens?
choices: Both updates are applied, and the refresh's new segment is merged in automatically.
compareAndSet fails, the loop re-reads the current snapshot and rebuilds the merge from it, so the refreshed segment is not lost.
The compaction overwrites the snapshot and the newly refreshed segment is dropped.
compact() throws an IllegalStateException because the snapshot changed.

questions.prompt: A writer thread's add() pushes the counter past refreshThreshold while another thread is already inside refresh(). What does that writer do?
choices: It blocks until the running refresh finishes, then runs its own refresh.
It runs a second refresh concurrently, since the buffer is a concurrent queue.
It throws an exception to signal back-pressure.
It returns right away without refreshing; its document stays buffered until a later refresh drains it.

questions.prompt: search() copies current.get() into a local variable and uses only that variable for the whole query. Why does that matter?
choices: It stops refreshes from running while a query is in progress.
The query sees one consistent set of segments and one generation number even if a new snapshot is published mid-query.
It makes the AtomicReference read cheaper than reading the field twice.
It guarantees the query sees documents that were added just before it started.
